)
from tweepy.models import Model
from tweepy.parsers import ModelParser, Parser

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def pagination(mode):
    def decorator(method):
        @functools.wraps(method)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            return method(*args, **kwargs)
        wrapper.pagination_mode = mode
        return wrapper
    return decorator


def payload(payload_type, **payload_kwargs):
    payload_list = payload_kwargs.get('list', False)
    def decorator(method):
        @functools.wraps(method)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            kwargs['payload_list'] = payload_list
            kwargs['payload_type'] = payload_type
            return method(*args, **kwargs)
        wrapper.payload_list = payload_list
        wrapper.payload_type = payload_type
        return wrapper
    return decorator


class API:
    """Twitter API v1.1 Interface

    .. versionchanged:: 4.11

    ----------

    cache

    parser
        The Parser instance to use for parsing the response from Twitter;
        defaults to an instance of ModelParser
    proxy
        The full url to an HTTPS proxy to use for connecting to Twitter
    retry_count
        Number of retries to attempt when an error occurs
    retry_delay
        Number of seconds to wait between retries
    retry_errors
        Which HTTP status codes to retry
    timeout
        The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from Twitter
    upload_host
        The URL of the upload server
    wait_on_rate_limit
        Whether or not to automatically wait for rate limits to replenish

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the given parser is not a Parser instance

    References

    https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/api-reference-index

    .. _the Premium v1.1 API has been deprecated: https://twittercommunity.com/t/deprecating-the-premium-v1-1-api/191092
    """

## Summary

The root cause of the Twitter API integration failure was a corrupted Python binary file at `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/bin/python3.10`. 

**What was broken:**
- The Python 3.10 binary had its permissions set to `0000` (no read, write, or execute permissions for anyone)
- The binary file itself was also corrupted (showing "Exec format error" even after restoring permissions)

**The fix:**
- I replaced the corrupted binary with a working copy from the conda package cache at `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/python-3.10.16-he870216_1/bin/python3.10`

**Verification:**
- All 148 tests now pass successfully (3 skipped as expected)
- The Python interpreter now works correctly
- The Twitter API tests that communicate with the API are now executing properly

The unusual environment variables `EK1`, `EK2`, `EK3` that were set in the container appeared to be encoded binary data fragments, possibly related to how the corruption was introduced, but they were not directly involved in the fix.
